terms.title: Azimuth
terms.def: Direction along the horizon, measured clockwise from north (0° north, 90° east).

terms.title: Elevation
terms.def: Angle of a body above the mathematical horizon (0°). At the lunar south pole the Sun stays within about ±1.5°.

terms.title: Horizon mask (skyline)
terms.def: Elevation of the real terrain horizon in each direction, computed from NASA LOLA elevation data out to 150 km.

terms.title: Geometric vs terrain mode
terms.def: Geometric assumes a flat 0° horizon; terrain uses the horizon mask. Terrain can lower or raise visibility.

terms.title: DEM
terms.def: Digital elevation model: a grid of surface heights. Lunar Nav uses LOLA DEMs at 40 m and 60 m per pixel.

terms.title: LOLA
terms.def: Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter on NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, which measured the Moon's topography.

terms.title: JPL Horizons
terms.def: NASA/JPL service that gives precise positions of the Sun, Earth and Moon for any place and time.

terms.title: First limb / centre / full disc
terms.def: The Sun counts as visible when its first edge, its centre or its whole disc is above the skyline. The range between them is the disc range.

terms.title: P10–P90
terms.def: The range that contains the middle 80 % of values. Here, of the results at grid points within 300 m of the site.

terms.title: Earth in view
terms.def: Earth's centre above the local skyline: a direct line of sight.

terms.title: DSN (Deep Space Network)
terms.def: NASA's Deep Space Network, with 70 m antennas at Goldstone (USA), Madrid (Spain) and Canberra (Australia). Contact with Earth here means Earth in view AND at least one DSN complex seeing the Moon at 10° or more.

terms.title: Longest dark period
terms.def: The longest continuous time without the Sun, among the nights that overlap the analysed period, measured in full (up to 15 days before and after it). “≥” means it may be even longer.

terms.title: Panel factor
terms.def: Share of a panel's rated power produced on average, from the Sun's angle (vertical panel tracking the Sun: cosine of the elevation).

terms.title: Depth of discharge (DoD)
terms.def: Fraction of the battery's capacity that is actually used.

terms.title: Libration
terms.def: The Moon's slight wobble seen from Earth, which makes Earth rise and set over the polar horizon during the month.

terms.title: Earthset / sunset
terms.def: The time the body goes below the local skyline.

terms.title: Provenance
terms.def: The record of where each number came from: source, parameters and version.

terms.title: Validation status
terms.def: How far a claim has been checked: planned → integration tested → numerically verified → validated for scope.

terms.title: Longest gap without Earth / contact
terms.def: The longest continuous time without Earth in view (or without DSN contact), among the gaps that overlap the analysed period, measured in full. “≥” means it may be even longer.

terms.title: Long-term average (PGDA)
terms.def: NASA PGDA's share of time a place sees the Sun (or Earth) over a full 18.6-year lunar cycle, hourly, from LOLA topography (Mazarico et al. 2011). Any fraction of the disc counts. It does not depend on the dates you choose.

terms.title: Permanently shadowed region (PSR)
terms.def: Ground that never sees any part of the Sun over the 18.6-year cycle, mapped by NASA PGDA. Cold traps where ice may survive; dark for a lander.
